attributes.title: Preregistration: Block III Retention, Feedback and Learning - Theory of Everything Research Programme.
attributes.description:
This preregistration freezes the first confirmatory study for Experimental Block III of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. Block III separates three causal channels that are often grouped under broad labels such as memory or adaptation: policy-accessible retained state (R), within-episode observation-action feedback (F), and between-episode experience-dependent policy learning (L).

Seven hypotheses are tested separately. H3.1-H3.2 evaluate whether retained historical information is selectively useful when present observation is insufficient and whether intervention on that retained state causally changes later behaviour. H3.3-H3.4 evaluate whether genuine closed-loop feedback is selectively advantageous under post-onset unpredictable disturbance and whether its contribution degrades under preregistered timing and channel-integrity perturbations. H3.5-H3.6 evaluate whether between-episode parameter learning selectively adapts to changed behavioural mappings and produces persistent policy modification that survives freeze-after-adaptation. H3.7 evaluates whether R, F and L retain partly separable causal roles in the full eight-condition R x F x L factorial task matrix.

The study uses twenty held-out simulation seeds and confirmatory-only task variants that were not executed during development: the majority_three history task, the mixed_heldout disturbance family, and the rotate2_heldout and cycle_alt_heldout mapping changes. Serious bypasses are retained deliberately: augmented present-state observation can bypass retained state, accurate open-loop control can bypass feedback in predictable worlds, and an explicit contextual policy repertoire can bypass learning when mapping identity is supplied directly. Successful bypasses restrict necessity claims rather than being treated as anomalies.

Development-only pilots were used to validate implementation, analysis and pilot-informed thresholds. They are disclosed and excluded from confirmatory evidence. All seven confirmatory manifests, the twenty-seed registry, task definitions, interventions, bypasses, estimands, multiplicity handling and Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Suspend/Reject rules were frozen before confirmatory execution. No Block III confirmatory seed or confirmatory-only task variant had been executed when the protocol was frozen, and the software execution gate remains closed until this preregistration is public.

A positive result would support only experimentally separable causal contributions of retained state, online feedback and between-episode policy modification in the registered artificial task family. It would not establish general intelligence, explicit world modelling, counterfactual planning, reflective self-awareness or phenomenal consciousness.

Related experimental programme: Craggs, K. (2026), Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230.

344-2.value:
This study asks whether three candidate adaptive mechanisms make experimentally separable causal contributions under task conditions specifically requiring their nominated functions.

1. Retention specificity (H3.1): Does policy-accessible retained state improve performance selectively when task-relevant history is unavailable from the present observable state, rather than providing a generic advantage in matched Markov tasks?

2. Causal retained-state use (H3.2): Does targeted erasure, permutation, scrambling or controlled substitution of retained state after history formation but before action alter later history-dependent behaviour in the predicted direction?

3. Feedback specificity (H3.3): Does genuine closed-loop observation-action coupling outperform matched open-loop, yoked and robust-open alternatives specifically when disturbances are unpredictable after control onset?

4. Feedback timing and integrity (H3.4): Does performance degrade predictably as observation delay becomes dynamically consequential or the nominated feedback channel is masked, noised, made stale or structurally scrambled?

5. Learning specificity (H3.5): Does between-episode experience-dependent parameter updating provide a selective advantage when behavioural mappings change, while providing little or no advantage when the mastered mapping remains stable?

6. Persistent learning (H3.6): Does the adapted behavioural mapping persist after parameter updates are frozen, and is adaptation selectively impaired when the update pathway is disabled or randomised?

7. Mechanism separability (H3.7): In the full R x F x L design, do retention, feedback and learning retain distinct interactions with history requirement, disturbance unpredictability and mapping change respectively?

The study does not hypothesise that R, F and L form a necessary hierarchy. Serious bypass success is explicitly permitted and will scope any claim of necessity.

344-4.value: Data does not yet exist. No part of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists, and no part will be generated until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value:
Development-only simulations were conducted before preregistration to validate the software, identify implementation defects, construct serious controls and bypasses, and set pilot-informed confirmatory thresholds. Those development data will not be used in the confirmatory analysis.

The confirmatory study uses a separately frozen twenty-seed registry and task variants not executed during development. A machine-readable audit confirms that the confirmatory-only variant labels do not occur in any development trajectory or hardening result file. All confirmatory manifests and referenced configuration files are SHA-256 locked. The execution registry programmatically refuses confirmatory runs until a public preregistration has been recorded. Analysis code and decision thresholds were exercised only on development variants before the freeze.

value: Simulation study: Using existing or synthetic data to assess performance of a model, mimic operation of an existing or proposed system, or predict possible outcomes in a controlled context. This may include demonstration of methods, many varieties of modeling, prediction of policy impacts, simulating behavior or outcomes in a population, and other designs.

Direct inference on causal relationship(s): This study is intended to infer or estimate a causal relationship between two or more variables. It is designed specifically for the purposes of causal inference or identification.

344-38.value:
No human or animal subjects are involved. Bias control instead relies on preregistration, frozen held-out seeds and task variants, automated execution, provenance validation and machine-readable decision rules.

The confirmatory task variants and twenty-seed registry are frozen before execution. Development task variants are different from the decisive variants. The analysis script, thresholds, multiplicity correction and decision rules are frozen before any confirmatory outcomes are observed. Confirmatory execution is blocked by software until the public OSF registration exists. These procedures provide prospective separation between development and confirmatory evidence even though conventional investigator blinding is not applicable.

344-40.value:
The study is a controlled simulation experiment organised into seven linked confirmatory manifests covering H3.1-H3.7. The central architecture is a 2 x 2 x 2 factorial manipulation of policy-accessible retained state (R), within-episode feedback (F), and between-episode learning (L), supplemented by targeted mechanism-specific intervention studies.

Retention is evaluated using matched history-dependent and present-state Markov tasks. Feedback is evaluated using matched predictable and post-onset unpredictable disturbances and closed-loop, open-loop, yoked and robust-open controllers. Learning is evaluated using stable and changed behavioural mappings with learning-enabled, frozen, randomised-update and contextual-bypass controls. The full factorial study evaluates all eight R x F x L combinations on matched mechanism-requiring and control tasks.

Conditions are paired within seed wherever appropriate. The independently seeded simulation replicate is the inferential unit. No human-subject counterbalancing is applicable.

344-44.value: No human or treatment randomisation is performed. Stochastic simulation variation is controlled by the frozen twenty-seed registry. Each registered seed is evaluated under the matched conditions required by the corresponding manifest so that primary contrasts are paired by seed.

344-47.value:
All confirmatory data will be generated prospectively by deterministic software plus registered pseudo-random seeds after the preregistration becomes public. Twenty unique held-out seeds are frozen before execution. Each seed is applied to all matched architecture/task conditions specified in a manifest.

Retention specificity uses 6,000 trials per registered seed/condition. Retention causal/profile tests use 7,000 trials. Feedback episodes use an 80-step horizon. Learning uses 80 calibration episodes, 160 adaptation episodes and 60 post-freeze evaluation episodes. The factorial study evaluates all eight R x F x L architectures for every registered seed.

Runs are accepted only when provenance validation passes. A technical failure does not count as a scientific outcome and may be rerun only using the same frozen manifest and seed, with the failed attempt retained as an audit trace.

344-51.value:
The confirmatory sample is 20 independent simulation seeds for every preregistered manifest. Matched architecture and intervention conditions are evaluated within each seed. The full factorial component therefore evaluates all eight R x F x L architectures across the same twenty independent seeds.

Trial or episode counts within a seed are fixed by the environment configuration and are not treated as independent inferential replicates.

344-53.value: Twenty independent seeds provide a common confirmatory replication standard with the earlier programme blocks while allowing paired seed-level consistency criteria and uncertainty estimation. Development showed large, stable mechanism-specific contrasts, so the sample size is not selected by post-hoc power optimisation. The study prioritises independent replicate seeds and held-out task structure over treating thousands of within-seed trials as independent observations.

344-55.value:
Confirmatory data collection begins only after the OSF preregistration is public and the execution registry is formally unlocked. All twenty registered seeds and all conditions specified by each manifest will be run. There is no outcome-dependent early stopping.

Data collection ends when all preregistered seed-condition executions have completed with valid provenance or have been transparently classified as technically invalid. Failed technical runs may be rerun only unchanged and do not justify altering the scientific protocol.

344-62.value:
Primary measured outcomes include task accuracy; feedback regulation performance and mean absolute control error; retained information R(tau); causal retained-state effect Rcausal; late post-change learning accuracy; post-freeze accuracy; adaptation episode; seed-level mechanism-specific performance differences; and factorial specificity interactions.

Secondary measurements include bypass performance, full retention-lag profiles, all fixed feedback perturbation effects, Holm-adjusted perturbation-family p-values and paired bootstrap confidence intervals.

344-71.value:
Primary inference is based on predeclared paired seed-level contrasts and fixed decision thresholds. Paired bootstrap 95% confidence intervals use 10,000 resamples with analysis RNG seed 20261008.

For H3.7, the full factorial analysis estimates effects of R, F and L and their mechanism-by-task-requirement interactions. The decisive quantities are R x history requirement, F x disturbance unpredictability, and L x mapping change. Interaction values are interpreted only on the registered performance scale.

For H3.4, intact-minus-perturbed performance is evaluated across the ten fixed channel perturbations. One-sided paired sign tests are computed at the seed level and adjusted as one preregistered family using the Holm procedure. Delay-2, delay-4 and sign scrambling are the primary perturbations for the decision criterion.

No individual within-seed trial is treated as an independent replicate for primary inference.

344-75.value: Binary mechanism factors R, F and L are coded 0/1. Task requirements are coded as matched binary contrasts. Accuracy and regulation performance remain on their natural [0,1] scales. Paired differences and pre-declared interaction contrasts are calculated directly. No outcome-dependent transformation or normalising composite score is planned.

344-77.value:
The exact numerical criteria are frozen in the seven manifests and formal preregistration record. In summary:
- H3.1 requires selective retention advantages >=0.30 at each registered lag, seed-level consistency, negligible Markov advantage and long-delay R1 accuracy >=0.80.
- H3.2 requires high intact performance, chance-level erase/permutation outcomes, strongly reversed opposite-state substitution, retained information at the longest lag and causal effects across the entire lag profile.
- H3.3 requires >=0.20 mean closed-loop advantage over every serious control under unpredictable disturbance, seed-level consistency and near-equivalence under predictable disturbance.
- H3.4 requires ordered delay degradation, minimum effect sizes for delay-4, stale-4 and sign scrambling, plus Holm-adjusted primary perturbation tests <0.05.
- H3.5 requires >=0.90 learning-enabled late accuracy and >=0.50 learner-minus-frozen advantage for each held-out mapping, with negligible stable-mapping advantage.
- H3.6 requires >=0.90 post-freeze performance, failure of frozen/randomised update controls to adapt equivalently, and timely adaptation in at least 18/20 seeds.
- H3.7 requires mean specificity interactions >=0.30 (retention), >=0.20 (feedback) and >=0.50 (learning), seed-level consistency, and negligible mechanism effects in the matched control tasks.
Each hypothesis receives one of Retain, Restrict, Reduce, Suspend or Reject. The mechanisms also receive separate overall scoped judgements; there is no single Block III adaptation score.

344-79.value:
Every registered seed is included if the run is provenance-valid. No scientific outlier exclusion is planned. Extreme values produced by valid simulations remain part of the evidence.

A run is invalid only for preregistered technical reasons: manifest/configuration validation failure, non-finite or incomplete required output, or failed provenance/integrity validation. Invalid technical runs are reported separately rather than silently excluded.

344-81.value: No imputation is planned. A technically invalid or incomplete run is not converted into a scientific value. It may be rerun only with the unchanged manifest and seed, retaining the failed attempt as an audit artefact. If a registered condition cannot be completed validly, the affected hypothesis may be suspended rather than analysed on an opportunistically reduced sample.

344-83.value:
Serious bypasses will be reported explicitly. Success of the augmented-observation retention bypass, robust predictable open-loop control, or contextual static learning bypass will be interpreted as evidence against universal necessity, not as a reason to erase a mechanism-specific causal effect in environments where the bypass information is absent.

Additional interaction terms in the eight-condition factorial design may be reported descriptively, but they will not replace the preregistered mechanism-by-requirement interactions or be labelled emergence/synergy without a separate preregistered interpretation.

344-86.value:
Block III follows completed Blocks I and II but does not assume that retention, feedback or learning follows necessarily from self-maintenance or selection. Experimental implementation order is methodological rather than an asserted ontological hierarchy.

The study is deliberately narrow. Even full retention of H3.1-H3.7 would show only that policy-accessible retained state, within-episode feedback and between-episode learning make partly separable causal contributions in the registered artificial task family. It would not establish general intelligence, explicit world models, counterfactual planning, reflective self-awareness or phenomenal consciousness.

The complete preregistration package contains the frozen manifests and locks, held-out seed registry, confirmatory task configurations, intervention/bypass registry, source code, analysis code, tests, seed/held-out audits and development-validation records.
